# LoopBridge: Should Prefill and Decode Loop Equally?

> Looped (recurrent-depth) language models use the same number of loops to read the prompt (prefill) and to generate
> each answer token (decode), although generation is almost all decoding. We untie the two loop counts (prefill m
> loops, decode n < m) and introduce LoopBridge (2.4% of the parameters: decoder LoRA + RoPE-commuting per-loop
> key/value maps), a single adapter distilled from the four-loop model that serves every trained (m, n) pair and folds
> into the prompt cache once at prefill. (A restricted fixed-m=4 decoder-only LoRA variant is documented in Appendix L.)
> Evaluated on Ouro-2.6B, Ouro-1.4B, Thinking models and Lev decision models. Every number is recomputed from released
> per-item scores by ouro/scripts/paper_numbers.py.

Main findings (Ouro-2.6B; 95% paired bootstrap intervals in the paper):
- At batch 1, prefill is 0.3-2.6% of the wall time of a chain-of-thought request (0.1-0.3% on Thinking models).
- One decode loop: LoopBridge 4/1 raises the 11-benchmark average from 44.2 (Original 1/1) to 58.2 (58.3 +- 0.1 over
  three seeds), above tied-loop distillation on the same data (49.5; rank 80: 49.3); at two decode loops, 63.7 -> 69.1
  (vs 66.2 Distilled 2/2); MATH-500 zero-shot.
- Measured time (800 requests, batch 1): LoopBridge 4/1 scores 45.0% (+17.2 over Original 1/1, +10.8 over Distilled 1/1)
  at 27.7 tokens/s (vs 28.3 for Original 1/1) and +10.5 points over a time-matched Original 1/1-2/2 mix; 4/2 runs at
  14.3 tokens/s (2.1x Original 4/4). At batch 32, LoopBridge 4/1 stays +18.5 / +11.3 points ahead in 1.18x / 1.19x time.
- The gain peaks within two to five prefill loops (also for an adapter trained to 16 loops, over seeds, and with the
  prefill loops trained too).
- Transfers to Ouro-1.4B (44.5 at 4/1, 44.2 +- 0.2 over three seeds, vs 40.5 distilled and 34.7 original),
  Ouro-2.6B-Thinking (4/2 within 0.8 points of 4/4 on average and +3.1 above Distilled 2/2; served in batches, matches
  Original 4/4 on all 1,319 GSM8K problems at 2.0x throughput and 0.47-0.57x wall time) and Lev decision models.
- Baselines: the distilled controls move by at most 0.8 points over 0.3x-3x learning rates and at rank 80.

Limitations stated by the author: timing on one GPU type at batch 1 to 32; folded maps keep one prompt cache per decode
loop (the one-cache LoopBridge keeps one cache but applies its maps at every decode step, which costs decode time); the prefill depth is fixed per setting; models up to 3B with
four loops; English benchmarks.

## Docs
- README.md: findings, when to use, repository map
- REPRODUCE.md: every table and figure -> script -> result file; training and evaluation commands
- paper/untying-prefill-decode-loops.pdf: the paper
- ouro/results/items/: per-item scores of every run the paper uses; ouro/results/paper_numbers.json: the recomputed statistics
- ouro/results/provenance/: command, configuration, checkpoint hash, log and outputs of every run
- ARCHIVE.md: where the training checkpoints, raw evaluation outputs and prepared data are kept (private archive)
- DEPRECATED.md: the modules and training arms the paper does not use
- The tag paper-arxiv is the commit the arXiv version was built from; the project finished on 2026-11-19.
